name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+19 partisan lean
Incumbent Glenn Thompson seeking re-election with large financial edge
Minimal Democratic challenger resources and no outside spending
No public polling; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Thompson holds a heavily Republican seat, a 10-to-1 fundraising advantage, and incumbency benefits, while markets price him near 95% to win. No polling or ratings contradict the fundamentals, so the safe-Republican assessment stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the challenger within single digits, or a major scandal involving the incumbent, would be the main reason to revisit this call.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 15th District leans strongly Republican, with a partisan advantage of about 19 points toward the GOP. Glenn Thompson, the incumbent, is running for re-election and has raised over $2 million, holding more than $700,000 on hand. His Democratic challenger, Ray Bilger, has raised roughly $210,000 with little cash remaining, and neither side shows meaningful outside spending.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets price Thompson's chances at about 95 percent. The combination of a deep-red seat, an entrenched incumbent, and a heavily outspent challenger makes this a safe Republican hold, with only modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
